repo.name: souffle
repo.description: Soufflé is a variant of Datalog for tool designers crafting analyses in Horn clauses. Soufflé synthesizes a native parallel C++ program from a logic specification.

readme.summary: README effectively explains what Soufflé is and lists features comprehensively, but lacks practical examples, quick start code, and detailed installation/configuration guidance.
readme.top_issue: No code examples showing basic Soufflé/Datalog syntax or usage patterns - users must click through to external documentation to see what the language actually looks like

injection_risks.description: The executeBinaryAndExit function executes a binary file using the system's default shell, which can lead to command injection attacks if the binary filename is not properly sanitized.
The compileToBinary function constructs a command string using user-provided input (command, sourceFilenames), which can lead to command injection attacks if the input is not properly sanitized.

critical_findings: Potential command injection vulnerability in executeBinaryAndExit
Potential command injection vulnerability in compileToBinary
security.summary: The Souffle codebase has some security concerns, including potential command injection vulnerabilities and lack of input validation, but no hardcoded secrets or critical error exposure issues were found.

common_complaints: Correctness bugs in subsumption and optimization transformations
Ungrounded variable error messages and assertion failures
Build compatibility issues across architectures (x86, Fedora 42)
praise_themes: Recognition of project power and capabilities
